sections.content:
The Pakistan Rangers are a paramilitary force under the Ministry of Interior, organised into two wings: the Punjab Rangers and the Sindh Rangers. They guard the eastern border with India, support the police in maintaining law and order, and assist in internal security duties, including protecting sensitive installations and helping during emergencies.

Both wings recruit separately and advertise vacancies in national newspapers, with province-wise quotas so that candidates from each province get a fair share of posts. Sindh Rangers applications are submitted through the official portal join.pakistanrangerssindh.gov.pk, while Punjab Rangers announcements appear in the press and on the force's official channels.
sections.title: Two wings: Punjab Rangers and Sindh Rangers

sections.content:
The main posts are Sub Inspector, Havaldar, Naik, Sepoy General Duty and Sepoy Clerk. Sub Inspectors need a graduation degree and must be aged 20 to 28 years. Havaldars need Intermediate education, while Naik and Sepoy GD need Matric. Sepoy Clerks need Matric plus typing skills.

The general age limit for most posts is 18 to 30 years, though the exact range is given in each recruitment advertisement. The September 2026 Punjab Rangers drive advertised 205 posts across several ranks. Candidates should always check the official advertisement for the exact age, education and quota details of their province.
sections.title: Posts, education and age limits

sections.content:
Male candidates must be at least 5 feet 6 inches tall, with a chest measurement of 33 inches and 1.5 inches of expansion. Female candidates need a minimum height of about 5 feet 4 inches. These standards are checked at the physical measurement stage, and candidates who fail them cannot proceed further.

The physical test includes a 1.6 kilometre (one mile) run, which male candidates are generally expected to complete in about 8 minutes. The run tests stamina and fitness for the demanding duties of the force. Candidates who pass the physical test move on to the written test, so regular running practice before applying is essential.
sections.title: Physical standards and the running test

sections.content:
The written test covers Urdu, English, Mathematics, general knowledge and Islamiat. It checks basic academic ability rather than advanced subjects, so candidates who prepare from Matric-level material usually do well. Marks in the written test, combined with the physical test, decide who is shortlisted for interview.

Shortlisted candidates go through a detailed medical examination and an interview before final selection. Selected recruits then complete basic training of four to six months, covering drill, weapons handling, physical training, border duties and discipline. After training, Rangers are posted to border areas or internal security duties across the country.
